# Results — Study 379 (ETF Lead-Lag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The microstructure folklore —
**the big liquid ETF leads its slow members by a day** — tested on **daily** bars. We use
**SPY** as the leader and an equal-weight **basket of 37 smaller, less-liquid US members** as
the laggards, build daily log returns, and ask whether *yesterday's* leader move predicts
*today's* member move (a lead-lag cross-correlation profile) and whether a next-bar rule (long
the laggards the day after a big-leader day) survives one-way costs. Offline & deterministic;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + a fixed 37-name smaller/less-liquid US basket (public, no key) |
| Window | 2000-01-04 → 2026-06-18 (**6,654** trading days; **26.5** years) |
| Returns | daily **log** returns; laggard basket = equal-weight mean of member returns each day |
| Signal day | leader (SPY) return in the **top decile** (q ≥ 0.90); rule enters the basket on the **next** bar |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; one-way 5 bps each side ⇒ 10 bps round-turn per 1-day trade |

> **Daily-bar caveat (named on the Signal axis).** True lead-lag in microstructure lives at
> the **intraday / tick** scale, which is **not** on yfinance (daily OHLCV only). On daily
> bars a one-session lead would have to be large to survive — and it isn't here. The basket is
> a fixed set of **surviving** smaller names (mild survivorship, named on the axis), and 3
> originally-listed members (`SEE`, `IPG`, `JNPR`) had no usable history and were dropped. The
> verdict does **not** hinge on the exact basket: the next-day signal is **absent-to-negative**
> by every measure below.

## The lead-lag profile — where is the predictability?

corr(leader\_{t−k}, members\_t) for k = −5..+5. **k = 0** is the contemporaneous co-movement
(today's leader vs today's members); **k = +1** is the tradable claim (yesterday's leader
*predicts* today's members).

| k (lag) | −1 | **0** | **+1** | +2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr | −0.051 | **+0.867** | **−0.048** | −0.012 |

Read it carefully. The members move **with** the leader **contemporaneously** — a massive
**+0.87** at k = 0. That is real, and it is **untradable**: you cannot act on a move that
happens *the same day* you'd need to already know it. The believers' tradable claim lives at
**k = +1** (yesterday's leader → today's members), and there the correlation is **−0.048** —
essentially zero, and if anything mildly **negative** (a faint next-day *reversal*, the
opposite of a lead).

## The one-day lead-lag slope — HAC-robust, and it points the wrong way

OLS of members\_t on leader\_{t−1}, Newey-West (5-lag) HAC standard error:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope (members on lagged leader) | **−0.058** |
| HAC *t* | **−1.88** |
| n | 6,653 |

The one-day lead-lag slope is **negative** at HAC *t* = −1.88 — not a positive lead, a mild
**reversal**, and not significant either. There is no statistically real next-day lead from
the leader to the members on daily bars.

## The next-bar rule — long the laggards after a big-leader day

1-day entry lag; the unconditional column is *all* daily member returns (the base rate). Welch
*t* compares the conditional next-day mean to the unconditional mean; the placebo *p* is the
share of 20,000 random same-size next-day draws whose mean **beats** the conditional set.

| q | n trades | cond. next-day mean | cond. win-rate | base mean | base win-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.90 | 666 | **−0.078%** | 50% | +0.029% | 52% | **−1.34** | 0.969 |
| 0.95 | 333 | **−0.102%** | 51% | +0.029% | 52% | **−1.03** | 0.945 |

The conditional next-day member return after a big-leader day is **below** the base rate, at
**t = −1.34** with **placebo p = 0.97** — i.e. the conditional mean sits at the *bottom* of the
luck cloud (97% of random next-day draws do **better**). The "buy the slow members after the
leader pops" rule does not even point up.

## Costs — they only deepen a hole that is already negative

| q | n trades | gross mean | net @ 5 bps one-way (10 bps round-turn) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.90 | 666 | −0.078% | **−0.178%** |
| 0.95 | 333 | −0.102% | **−0.202%** |

The rule loses money **gross**; a realistic 10 bps round-turn on a one-day hold turns a small
loss into a bigger one. There is no cost regime that makes a **negative** gross edge tradable.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (edge=0 quiet, planted lead lights up)

Deterministic leader/member returns with a **planted one-day lead** knob ``lead`` (the fraction
of yesterday's leader move that leaks into today's members), seed 379, 6,000 days:

| planted `lead` | xcorr k=+1 | lag-1 slope | HAC *t* | rule cond. | rule base | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no lead) | +0.011 | +0.014 | 0.83 | +0.071% | +0.044% | 0.49 | 0.297 |
| **0.05** (small) | +0.050 | +0.064 | **3.76** | +0.162% | +0.047% | **2.03** | 0.015 |
| **0.25** (large) | +0.202 | +0.264 | **15.48** | +0.523% | +0.060% | **8.18** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted lead the profile, the HAC slope and the next-bar rule all stay quiet
(HAC *t* = 0.83, rule *t* = 0.49 — no false positive). A **small** planted lead (0.05) is
detected at HAC *t* = 3.8 and a tradable rule *t* = 2.0; a **large** one screams. The control
proves the machinery would **find** a real lead if one existed — and on the real daily tape it
finds **none**.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The only large correlation is **contemporaneous** (+0.87 at k = 0) and
  **untradable** by construction. The one-day lead the claim needs is **absent**: xcorr at
  k = +1 is **−0.048**, the HAC lag-1 slope is **−0.058 (t = −1.88)**, and the conditional
  next-day return is **below** the base rate (t = −1.34, placebo p = 0.97). No predictive lead
  on daily bars. (True lead-lag is an intraday phenomenon, named on the axis — but the *daily*
  version believers point to does not exist here.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The next-bar rule is **negative gross** (−0.078%/trade) and worse
  net of a 10 bps round-turn (−0.178%). You cannot deploy a rule whose edge points the wrong
  way before you even pay to trade it.
- **"Free lunch — the leader hands you the members"? — BUSTED.** The co-movement that *looks*
  like a free lunch is **same-day**: by the time you can act, the move has already happened.
  The only thing left to trade — the next-day lead — is statistically zero on daily bars. The
  "slow members catch up tomorrow" story is real intraday and **gone by the daily close**.
